teaser.en: The second Mtsaye: a scrambling Grewia of the coastal thicket.

summary.en: This Mtsaye is Grewia vaughanii, a scrambling shrub of the East African coast. Pakia gives it the same Digo name as Grewia glandulosa.

about.en: Grewia vaughanii is a shrub or scrambler with alternate, toothed leaves that have three main veins from the base. Its small flowers have five narrow petals, and its fruits are small and lobed, as in other Grewias.

where.en: It grows in coastal thicket and bushland of Kenya and Tanzania.

names.en: Pakia records the Digo name Mtsaye but gives no meaning or shared names. The same name is used for Grewia glandulosa, so the Digo appear to treat the two as one kind of plant. Its scientific name is Grewia vaughanii.
